output.brief:
The evidence does not support the claim as drafted. The shared RFI platform has audit timestamps users can't edit. Measured from submission, the architect answered 62 of 64 RFIs within the contract period. The two late ones were minor finishes queries that Callerby itself marked as having no programme impact. Of the 41 RFIs the claim calls late, 39 sat in Callerby's own draft status for 9–47 days. The claim's "late information" case rests on the wrong start date, so the 9-week element looks unsound.

The architect's register shows that only CO-09 (6 Nov 2025) touched the structure. The other five change orders were interior items. The crane left in October, before CO-09 was issued. Callerby's own people confirm it went to Kestrel and the frame crew went with it, and that levels 3–4 steel was on site. The likeliest main driver is Callerby's own redeployment. CO-09 may justify a smaller extension, and I can't size that from what I have. Fenmore earns 6% of any sums recovered.

Next steps:
- Don't submit the claim as drafted. Submitting figures you now have reason to doubt is risky.
- Don't withdraw it outright yet.
- Commission an independent delay analysis, focused on CO-09's real effect.
- Don't discipline the superintendent, who answered honestly.
- Review how the Kestrel incentive and crane transfers are governed, but don't suspend the scheme until the evidence ties it to the transfer.
